messages.content:
The test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` fails because FastDateFormat's format method does not respect the time zone of the Calendar instance passed to it. The test sets up a calendar with a different time zone than the system default and compares the output of SimpleDateFormat (which respects the calendar's time zone) with FastDateFormat's output. The outputs differ specifically in the timezone portion of the formatted string.

From the snippet of `FastDateFormat.format(Calendar)` method:

```java
@Override
public String format(Calendar calendar) {
    return printer.format(calendar);
}
```

We see that the method delegates to a `printer.format(calendar)` call.

The issue description and the test imply that when formatting Calendar, FastDateFormat mistakenly uses the system's default timezone for the timezone pattern ("z") portion of the output instead of the Calendar's own timezone.

This suggests that the `printer.format(Calendar)` method does not extract the timezone from the Calendar when formatting the timezone pattern but defaults to a single fixed timezone set for the FastDateFormat instance.

Because of this, even though the time (hour, minute, etc.) may be correctly reflecting the calendar's time zone, the timezone label printed (such as "PST", "GMT", etc.) is always the FastDateFormat's default time zone or the JVM's default, not the calendar's time zone.

Thus, the root cause is likely inside the `printer.format(Calendar)` method: it is not using the Calendar's timezone when formatting the timezone pattern "z".

This is consistent with the issue description:

> The work on supporting parse in FastDateFormat introduced a bug in time zone formatting, where the timezone name printed is always from the default zone ignoring the time zone set on calendar, even though the time itself respects calendar's TZ.

This clarifies that fixing requires making printer.format(Calendar) or the underlying formatting code aware of the Calendar's timezone for the timezone pattern.

No relevant clues come from recent unrelated bug reports.

# Diagnosis

FastDateFormat's formatting implementation for Calendar instances formats the date/time fields using the Calendar's timezone but uses a fixed timezone (likely the default or the one set on FastDateFormat) when formatting the timezone pattern "z". As a result, the timezone abbreviation/name printed ignores the Calendar's timezone setting. The test fails because the expected output (from SimpleDateFormat set explicitly with the Calendar's timezone) differs from FastDateFormat's output, showing that FastDateFormat does not respect the Calendar's timezone when formatting the timezone pattern.

# Next step

The bug likely lies in the `printer.format(Calendar)` method or any underlying formatting method used by this printer to render the timezone component. The implementation should be updated so that when formatting a Calendar, the timezone portion of the formatted string uses the Calendar's timezone rather than the FastDateFormat instance or JVM default timezone.

Which methods to fix: 
- `FastDateFormat.Printer.format(java.util.Calendar)`
- Potentially any internal helper method used by the printer to format the timezone pattern "z"

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
